text:
Git branching is a powerful feature of the version control system Git, allowing developers to work on new ideas without disrupting the main codebase. Instead of committing directly to the main branch, you create a separate feature branch for each new task or improvement. This keeps the primary project stable while you experiment.

Once your work on the feature branch is complete, you typically request a review through a pull request. Team members can comment on your code and suggest changes. After approval, you merge the branch back into the main branch. This structured workflow ensures that all contributions are tested and reviewed, making collaboration smoother and reducing the risk of errors in the final product.
